findings.statement: The fixed dimensionless-lattice ME-DVM subroute is rejected, but no universal moving-lattice/remap no-go is proved. The strongest fair response is the exact witness delta_y(T)=m_e/(64T), which keeps the mass index equal to 64 and evades the fixed-spacing integrality obstruction; conditionally, an exactly on-shell reversible edge network with nonnegative symmetric conductances could provide invariants, detailed balance, Pauli-compatible positivity, and an eventwise fermionic H-theorem. The response remains non-admitted because no registered theorem transports occupations while preserving exact invariants, reversibility, positivity, entropy, differentiability, permutation covariance, full-half-line tail closure, and deterministic finite edge structure across continuous temperature. This is an evidence-bounded INCONCLUSIVE candidate verdict, not an impossibility theorem.
assumptions_used: Temperature varies on a nondegenerate continuous interval.
Fixed-lattice exact closure requires the registered mass-index integrality condition.
A moving spacing is only a scope witness until a structure-preserving remap theorem and complete edge graph exist.
All candidate and common G-EXT-FEASIBILITY obligations remain binding.
counterevidence_refs: The exact moving-spacing witness defeats any inference from the two-temperature fixed-lattice test to all moving-remap designs.
A future sparse deterministic edge construction and structure-preserving remap theorem could reverse the current non-admission.
reproduction: Read A-EXT01-SAGE findings F-EXT01-SAGE-002 and F-EXT01-SAGE-003 together; their scopes are fixed lattice and moving remap respectively.
Read A-EXT01-ROCQ finding F-ROCQ-004 and compare its missing dependencies with CAS_CONTRACT candidate C-MEDVM.

Prospective conditioning, binary64, LOC, and net-deletion certificates.

findings.statement: No candidate establishes exact non-isomorphism to sealed B3-v2. The compactified candidates plausibly change three mechanisms: full-half-line compactification instead of finite Y_max plus a tail ledger, local trial/test or analytic-direct-sum ownership instead of the global B3 polynomial basis, and one generated operation graph instead of split source/vector/oracle authority. MEDVM would be structurally distinct if its full moving edge/remap graph existed. These are fair novelty hypotheses, but no complete candidate operator and no bidirectional operation-DAG comparison exist, so neither isomorphism nor non-isomorphism is proved. A coordinate, basis, language, or compiler change alone is insufficient.
assumptions_used: Novelty is assessed against B3-v2 basis, finite-domain/tail ledger, mass solve, event trace, and A0-A4 graph as a whole.
A complete operator and consumer graph is necessary for an exact non-isomorphism certificate.
Missing novelty proof is INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence of sameness.
counterevidence_refs: A unified analytic full-half-line representation or a complete moving finite-state edge graph could be genuinely non-isomorphic once fully specified.
reproduction: Compare the three named sibling findings against the CAS_CONTRACT novelty obligation without inspecting any unregistered result.
unresolved: Complete candidate operator and consumer graph.
Exact bidirectional operation-DAG isomorphism or non-isomorphism certificate.

findings.statement: The registered cost screen is not passed by any candidate. SAGE reports ME-DVM dense-proxy counts of 34,504,704 edges for R=39,N_E=96,N_angle=1 and 621,084,672 for R=39,N_E=48,N_angle=12, an estimated 500-1000 design lines before evaluator code, and no credible same-change deletion plan. The compactified PCR-DG estimate of 800-1500 lines and possible net deletion of 600-1700 lines straddles both hard thresholds rather than proving permanent LOC<=800 and net deletion>=1000. These figures reject the registered cost claims as presented; they are not universal lower bounds, and a prospectively sealed sparse/factorized ME-DVM or exact compactified replacement diff could change the result.
assumptions_used: Permanent implementation estimate must be no greater than 800 LOC.
The same change must delete enough obsolete surface to yield at least net -1000 LOC.
Only registered estimates and deletion plans count; favorable ends of ranges are not silently selected.
Dense-proxy counts are candidate screens, not complexity lower bounds for every future factorization.
counterevidence_refs: The favorable endpoint of the compactified ranges could satisfy both thresholds, but no exact plan selects and proves it.
A sparse deterministic ME-DVM factorization could invalidate the dense proxy as an implementation estimate.
reproduction: Read A-EXT01-SAGE finding F-EXT01-SAGE-005 and apply the two literal CAS_CONTRACT cost thresholds.
unresolved: File-specific same-change deletion plan and net diff.
Deterministic sparse ME-DVM edge-count and operation-count theorem.

findings.statement: MANDATORY SEVEN-STAGE LOOP. (1) SELF-DISCOVER: the controlling question is candidate admission under all eleven binding obligations, not whether isolated endpoint, determinant, entropy, or fixed-lattice statements can be proved. (2) STEP-BACK: the same-space no-go and fixed-lattice obstruction are genuine bounded failures; the exact local determinant and eventwise entropy sign are genuine bounded passes; moving-remap, Petrov, and analytic-direct-sum feasibility remain candidate-level theorem gaps. (3) METACOGNITIVE SELF-ASK: theorem absence must not become a universal impossibility theorem, dense-edge proxies must not become complexity lower bounds, and axis vote counts must not replace the gate rule. (4) CoVe: SAGE, Rocq, and SymPy agree that the same-space wording fails, the fixed lattice does not generalize to a moving-remap no-go, complete novelty is unproved, and no candidate closes its full obligation set. Their top-level FAIL versus INCONCLUSIVE labels are not a substantive conflict: candidate feasibility is inconclusive while the binding gate fails because no candidate passes. Likewise, SAGE's fixed-lattice PASS obstruction and moving-remap INCONCLUSIVE finding address different scopes. (5) ADVERSARIAL SELF-ASK / STRONGEST OPPOSING STEELMAN: the strongest countercase is a compactified analytic direct sum with eta_0=-p/T plus terminal-vanishing perturbations, one non-bypassable full-half-line representation, and one generated DAG; it evades NC-SAME-SPACE and could in principle consolidate B3 surfaces. The moving-remap countercase is also live because delta_y(T)=m_e/(64T) defeats the fixed-spacing test and a nonnegative symmetric reversible edge network could inherit eventwise structure. (6) CCoT: either countercase reaches admission only through a complete operator, process-total finite-m_e shell, exact conservation and semidiscrete entropy, deterministic Jacobian/permutation semantics, uniform conditioning, prospective binary64 bound, exact non-isomorphism, and exact cost/deflation plan. The registered chain breaks at several independent links for every candidate. (7) PDR / STRONGEST STOP CASE: retain STOP/PRESERVE, archive all three candidates, and do not create PR-01. This conclusion is controlled by multiple missing binding obligations plus the actual same-space and fixed-lattice subroute failures, not by an overbroad impossibility claim. DECISIVE FALSIFIERS: a moving remap is terminally falsified by any demonstrated loss of exact reversibility, invariants, Pauli bounds, entropy, differentiability, tail closure, or cost closure; a compactified analytic candidate is terminally falsified by a singular coefficient map, bypassable/second tail consumer, or exact reduction to B3-v2. Conversely, the decisive falsifier of STOP/PRESERVE would be one prospectively sealed candidate artifact satisfying every candidate-specific and common obligation with no deferred branch or implementation choice. CONDITIONS THAT CHANGE THE VERDICT: such an artifact must include the complete operator/consumer graph, exact shell and entropy proofs, uniform <=1e6 condition or inf-sup certificate, prospective <=2.5e-11 binary64 certificate, exact non-isomorphism proof, <=800 permanent LOC estimate, and a same-change net deletion of at least 1000 LOC. Even then, implementation remains unauthorized until a separate explicit OWNER-1 decision.
